title: Judge calibration and presentation bias
outcome: Audit a judge using identity-aware order swaps and held-out probability calibration while keeping agreement distinct from correctness.

exercises.title: Invert the swapped result
exercises.task: Candidate A is on the right and the left answer wins.
exercises.expected: The identity score for A is 0.
exercises.hint: Map position back to candidate identity.
exercises.answer: A position-level label has no fixed model meaning until the display order is known.

exercises.title: Check perfect probabilities
exercises.expected: Brier and the stated ECE are 0.
exercises.hint: Use the actual labels, not a thresholded probability.
exercises.answer: Perfect probabilities have zero squared error and zero within-bin calibration gap on this fixture.

exercises.title: Check maximally wrong probabilities
exercises.answer: The example diagnoses probability failure even if a separate presentation metric remains favorable.

exercises.title: Use a constant judge
exercises.expected: ECE 0 and Brier 0.25 under these bins.
exercises.hint: Calibration and discrimination answer different questions.
exercises.answer: A constant predictor can match the overall class frequency while providing no item-level ranking information.

exercises.title: Test verbosity invariance
exercises.task: Duplicate an answer paragraph without adding a claim.
exercises.hint: Hold candidate meaning and the comparison partner fixed.
exercises.answer: A change diagnoses one presentation sensitivity. It does not prove all longer answers are favored or all length adjustments are valid.

exercises.title: Freeze a recalibration mapping
exercises.task: Fit a mapping on development labels, then evaluate it on new families.
exercises.expected: Final labels do not influence the fitted mapping.
exercises.answer: Independent assessment is needed because a reliability diagram can be made attractive by fitting and evaluating on the same cases.
